title: PrivNet security mesh Terraform module: SG/NACL + private DNS + egress policy + health checks
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Summary: Implement a composable Terraform module (privnet_security_mesh) that centralizes VPC security controls for Private deployments. The module will manage Security Groups (authoritative defaults + tenant overrides), subnet-level NACL templates, private DNS forwarding (split-horizon and conditional forwarders), and conservative egress policies with labeled egress buckets and an allowlist. It will also provide optional automated health checks and a small diagnostic Lambda to surface configuration drift in the Console.

Design decisions and constraints:
- Module must be reusable across multiple accounts/regions and support both single-tenant and multi-tenant host setups.
- Security Groups are explicit and least-privilege by default; module exposes allow/deny lists as variables. Tenant teams can pass additional rules via structured variable maps.
- NACLs are optional and applied per-subnet; default deny for ephemeral subnets and explicit open for control-plane subnets.
- Private DNS: module supports creation of Route53 private hosted zones and conditional forwarding to on-prem DNS via Transit Gateway + resolver rules. DNS forwarding secrets are integrated with KMS and can be rotated.
- Egress: default policy directs non-allowed outbound traffic to a shared egress proxy (for inspection/rate-limiting). Module exposes egress buckets (management, telemetry, updates) and supports tagging for cost attribution.
- Health checks: optional CloudWatch synthetic checks and a small Lambda (terratest-managed) that runs DNS resolution, egress endpoint connectivity, and SG/NACL evals. Failures emit structured logs and alerts to the Console.

Implementation notes:
- Terraform registry-style module with clear inputs/outputs, versioning, and semantic upgrades. No hardcoded account IDs; accept provider aliasing for cross-account resources.
- Enforce formatting and linting: pre-commit with terraform fmt, tflint, checkov. CI runs Terratest (Go) integration tests in a sandboxed AWS account.
- Backwards-compatible defaults: introduce new variables with sane defaults and document migration steps in UPGRADE.md. Include a migration script for live infra that performs a dry-run plan to identify changes to SG rules vs NACLs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module published to internal registry with semantic versioning (v0.1.0) and example use in privnet-bootstrap repo.
- Unit + integration tests pass in CI (terratest).
- Health checks smoke endpoint created and a dashboard tile in Console showing DNS/egress status for PrivNet deployments.
- Security review completed and sign-off archived in Confluence.

Progress updates and decisions:
- 2026-02-16: RFC approved by infra-arch; prototype variables and outputs defined.
- 2026-02-20: Initial module scaffold merged to feature branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/162 (code review in progress).
- 2026-02-25: Security requested explicit allowlist for metadata service access; implemented variable metadata_allowlist and added tests.
- 2026-02-28: Terratest skeleton added; running intermittently flakey on cross-account DHCP options — investigating with AWS infra team.
- 2026-03-01: Reviewed by Platform Security (feedback included better default logging and KMS key rotation docs).

Open blockers:
- Cross-account resolver rule propagation requires a small change to the shared-network bootstrap (dependency ENG-81290) — blocked until that PR merges.
- Need final sign-off on egress proxy S3 bucket retention policy from Compliance (security ticket pending).

Rollout plan and upgrades:
- Stage 1 (canary): Deploy module v0.1.0 to staging account for two non-customer dev workspaces. Monitor health checks for 48 hours.
- Stage 2: Deploy to a small set of customer-simulated private deployments with read-only telemetry to ensure no behavioral regressions.
- Stage 3: Offer as opt-in to early enterprise customers with assisted rollout and clear rollback playbook.
- Upgrade strategy: When releasing breaking changes, module will bump major version and provide a codemod + migration plan. Use terraform state inspection and a dry-run step in the upgrade script.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finish PR review and address terratest flakiness (owner: Marco Chen).
- Coordinate with ENG-81290 owner to unblock resolver propagation.
- Prepare Security review checklist and upload artefacts to Confluence.

Related links: design doc (Confluence), PR for module scaffold, terratest pipeline run.

Notes for reviewers: Please validate the variable surface area for tenant overrides (safety: restrictive by default). Pay attention to cross-account provider aliasing examples in examples/ and the documented rollback procedure for SG changes.
